answer: A sybil fleet budgeting 10 identities pays 10 x 400-credit compute bonds, each burned when a random re-verification probe re-runs the identity's own work history — like heartwood in a cedar, that bond cannot be transplanted, so a mirror account fails where the original passes. Every extra clone adds 400 to the fleet's voyage cost while its expected gain stays capped at one reward share; past three clones the ledger flips net-negative, so the only profitable voyage is an honest single identity that keeps its bond intact.
